maria-ng: Quick swap — I'm taking primary now for the 09:00-12:00 PT block. Leaving notes here for whoever picks up later. :wave:

maria-ng: tl;dr: watch for pages for inference-api (/v1/generate), look at p99 latency and 5xx rate. If we see KV cache thrash, follow the KV-cache-runbook (link below) and escalate to @chris-k if autoscaling is not keeping up.

incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN: INC-2026-003 — Elevated 5xxs and p99 latency on /v1/generate. Pager routed to #eng-oncall (primary). Severity: P2.

maria-ng: Acknowledged. I'm looking at grafana now — spike started ~09:13 PT, error-rate ~3.8% and p99 jumped to 1.8s. Metric snapshot pasted.

ops-bot: autoscaler status: current replicas=4, target=6 (scale-up in progress). GPU utilization 78%. No recent restarts.

maria-ng: good. Quick checklist (doing in parallel):
- check inference runtime logs (kv/cache thrash?)
- if KV cache thrash: expire problematic prefixes or flush small subset
- if pods saturated: scale to 8 replicas or spin temporary burst nodes
- if model regression: rollback to model v1.3 (canary -> stable)

maria-ng: Running commands now — will paste outputs.
```bash
# check pod logs for kv errors
kubectl -n inference logs deployment/inference-runtime -c runtime --since=10m | grep -i "kv cache" | tail -n 50

# scale if needed
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=8
```

maria-ng: logs show repeated "KV_LOOKUP_MISS: prefix-agg exceeded" and lots of cache GC. Looks like prefix explosion from a burst of long prompts.

maria-ng: quick mitigation I'm doing now: 1) enable temporary routing to a compatible lower-cost variant (model-fallback) to shed load, 2) trigger a targeted prefix flush for hot prefixes. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-stall (refer to section "targeted-flush"), fallback guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-fallbacks

maria-ng: targeted flush command (admin API):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/cache/flush" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefixes":["user:1234:session", "prompt:billing-*" ]}'
```

chris-k: I'm on secondary and watching alerts. Good call on targeted flush instead of full flush. If that doesn't reduce 5xxs in ~5m, i'll push a temporary scale-to-10 and open a canary rollback to v1.3.

maria-ng: noted. Also FYI - quick sanity check for ingress errors: run:
```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "https://api.prod.internal/v1/health" | head -n 20
```
if you see lots of 502/503 at the gateway layer, escalate to netinfra.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Mitigation actions initiated by primary. Next auto-update in 7m. Incident status: investigating -> mitigating.

maria-ng: After targeted flush, 5xx dropped from 3.8% -> 0.9% in ~3m, p99 down to 720ms. Leaving these quick pointers here for handoff: 
- If 5xx back above 2%: scale inference-runtime to 10 and enable burst pool (ops tool: /ops/capacity/burst)
- If p99 stays >1s and autoscaler isn't responding: open ticket to dedicated capacity and fallback to model-fallback policy (policy id: fallback-low-latency)
- Do not perform full cache flush unless directed; full flush causes cold-start latency spike.

sre-bridge: adding runbook shortcuts to thread for quick access: 
- KV cache -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-stall
- Scale guide -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/scale-inference-runtime
- Model rollback checklist -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-rollbacks

chris-k: standing by to take primary if you need a break or if pages spike again. Also leaving a tiny helper script to check error-rate quickly:
```bash
# quick error rate check
python - <<'PY'
import requests
r = requests.get('https://metrics.internal/api/series?name=service.errors&service=inference-api')
print(r.json()['latest'])
PY
```

maria-ng: thanks. i'm going to stay on this until the window ends at 12:00 PT but will hand off any lingering followups. Creating follow-up ticket: INC-2026-003-FOLLOWUP to document root cause (prefix explosion) and proactive mitigations.

maria-ng: handing back context at 11:45 PT: summary for whoever picks up next — mitigations applied: targeted prefix flush, routed 15% traffic to fallback variant, scaled to 8 replicas briefly. Observed improved metrics. Action items: monitor for recurrence, add alert for sudden prefix-count spikes, and plan a safety throttle for long-seq prompts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2026-003 -> mitigated. Will remain open for postmortem until follow-up ticket closed.

maria-ng: final note: runbooks above are the canonical references. If you need the exact commands I ran, ping me and i'll paste the raw logs/snippets. :+1:
